authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the limiting definition of a tangent line. Panel (a): a smooth curve in the xy-plane with a fixed point P and a moveable point Q marked on the curve; multiple pink secant lines through P fan outward, converging toward a limiting position labeled Tangent line, with arrows indicating the rotational approach to the limit. Panel (b): the same construction applied to a circle, showing P and Q on the circle with multiple secant lines rotating toward the tangent line at P. The figure establishes the general definition of a tangent line as the limiting position of secant lines as Q approaches P along the curve, and confirms that this definition agrees with the classical tangent to a circle.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag point Q along the curve toward fixed point P and watch the secant line rotate to become the tangent line, with the slope value updating in real time
- Toggle between panels (a) and (b) to compare the tangent-as-limit concept on a smooth open curve versus a circle
- Drag point P to a new position on the curve and observe how the tangent line direction changes
authoredContext: To obtain a definition of a tangent line that applies to curves other than circles, we must view tangent lines another way. For this purpose, suppose that we are interested in the tangent line at a point P on a curve in the xy-plane and that Q is any point that lies on the curve and is different from P. The line through P and Q is called a secant line for the curve at P. Intuition suggests that if we move the point Q along the curve toward P, then the secant line will rotate toward a limiting position. The line in this limiting position is what we will consider to be the tangent line at P (Figure 1.1.4a). As suggested by Figure 1.1.4b, this new concept of a tangent line coincides with the traditional concept when applied to circles.
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 1.1.4

discrepancies: the shaded purple wedge between the tangent and the current secant — the key visual showing the rotation toward the limit — is missing, replaced only by faint low-opacity ghost secant lines
the gray curved rotation arrows indicating the secant sweeping into the tangent are absent in both panels
panel (a)'s curve is a two-hump sinusoid, while the source shows a single smooth arch with P on the rising left side and Q on the descending right side
the 'Tangent line' leader line is a short floating gray segment that does not clearly connect the label to the tangent line, and in the screenshot it appears detached from any feature
the tangent at P in the source is steeply rising; in the generated figure the default tangent at P is nearly flat, weakening the visual drama of the rotation
evaluation.notes: Both source panels are correctly implemented behind a toggle with rich, working interactions (drag Q/P, slider, animate-to-limit, slope readouts), and the secant-to-tangent limit concept is accurately conveyed, but the signature shaded rotation wedge and curved arrows from the source are missing and the tangent label's leader line is visually detached.
action_items: Add the translucent purple filled wedge between the tangent line and the current secant line at P, plus the gray curved arrow arcs showing the secant rotating into the tangent
Fix the 'Tangent line' leader line so it visibly connects the label to the tangent line itself (anchor its endpoint on the line, e.g. at a point offset along the tangent from P)
Choose a default P location where the tangent is steep (e.g. tP ≈ 1.4 on the rising flank) so the fan of secants visibly rotates through a large angle as in the source
Replace the sinusoid with a single-arch curve (e.g. a downward parabola segment) to match panel (a)'s shape more closely
